evidence.snippet: We introduce PhAIL (Physical AI Leaderboard, https://phail.ai), an open real-robot benchmark on a Franka FR3 (dataset, per-rollout artifacts, and end-to-end reference implementation) of a distributional evaluation methodology: the time-to-success cumulative distribution function (CDF) as the evaluation primitive, with two separated jobs.

claire_radar.motivation: Real-world evaluation of vision-language-action (VLA) policies still rests on binary success rate at a fixed timeout with $N \le 25$ rollouts per condition, almost always without confidence intervals or paired statistical comparison; these cohort sizes struggle to resolve close comparisons reliably.

claire_radar.whyItMatters: It replaces binary success rates from small rollout counts with a distributional metric that includes confidence intervals and is anchored to human teleoperation. According to the abstract, this separates close VLA comparisons that threshold metrics cannot resolve.
